mechanism_narrative: A higher CPIAUCSL (inflation) compresses real equity valuations by increasing discount rates and real wage pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 190, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (exceeding 0.3 percentage points from the prior month) signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precede corporate earnings declines and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE increases by >0.3pp from prior month, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous expansion in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 3-month moving averages signals robust consumer demand and housing market strength, which typically drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when both RSAFS and HOUST exceed their 3-month moving averages, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply shock regime (defined as a 3-month decline in industrial production exceeding 1%), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate output and higher input costs.
regime_hint: supply shock regime (INDPRO decline > 1% over 3 months)
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO declines by >1% over 3 months, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that increases borrowing costs and dampens equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong residential construction activity and consumer confidence, which typically drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in less than 40% of periods when HOUST exceeds its 12-month moving average, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in industrial production exceeding 1% signals a manufacturing slowdown that reduces corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO declines by >1% over 3 months, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (exceeding 0.25 percentage points) and elevated inflation (CPIAUCSL above 200) signals a monetary policy response to overheating, which typically causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25pp and CPIAUCSL exceeds 200, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.
